- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.67) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤ 0.33) and forecast is elevated, apply downward bias correction to align with mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2 days above peak, then apply decay.  
- In 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; adjust downward by 2–5% for days 1–7 if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated high values followed by low values, model tends to lag; add 1–3% lag correction to forecast for the next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive but price declines, model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 3–5% for the next 3–5 days to avoid “sentiment reversal” bias.
